description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a beloved Middle Eastern comfort food, celebrated for its nourishing qualities and vibrant flavors. This hearty and aromatic soup, made with simple ingredients, offers a perfect blend of earthy lentils, fresh vegetables, and tangy lemon. It is a wonderfully warming and satisfying dish, ideal for any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Sauté Vegetables and Spices
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic, diced carrot, and diced potato to the pot. Sauté for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables start to soften slightly. Stir in the cumin powder and turmeric powder, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils, water or vegetable broth, salt, and black pepper to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend to Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Once cooked, you can leave the soup chunky or blend it for a smoother consistency. For a smooth soup, use an immersion blender directly in the pot, or carefully transfer portions to a regular blender and process until smooth. Be cautious when blending hot liquids.

instructions.title: Finish with Lemon
instructions.text: Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed. The lemon is crucial for the authentic Lebanese flavor, adding a bright, tangy finish.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or mint. Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges on the side and a drizzle of olive oil, if desired, alongside warm pita bread.

tips: For extra richness and depth, you can add a touch of dried mint along with the fresh mint garnish, or stir in a spoonful of tomato paste with the spices.
Do not skip the lemon juice at the end; it brightens the entire soup and is a signature flavor of Lebanese Adas. Adjust the amount to your personal preference.
This soup tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas (pronounced Ah-das), is more than just a dish; it's a hug in a bowl, a staple of Middle Eastern comfort food, and a testament to the power of simple, wholesome ingredients. This nourishing and flavorful soup holds a special place in Lebanese cuisine, cherished for its warming properties, affordability, and incredible taste. Whether it’s a chilly winter evening or you’re seeking a light yet satisfying meal, a bowl of Adas offers a delightful blend of earthy lentils, bright lemon, and aromatic garlic, often finished with a generous drizzle of olive oil.

Packed with protein and fiber, this naturally vegan and gluten-free soup is a testament to the fact that healthy eating can be utterly delicious and deeply satisfying. It’s a dish passed down through generations, embodying the spirit of Lebanese hospitality and the rich culinary heritage of the region. Get ready to discover the magic of Adas and bring a taste of the Levant into your kitchen.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a vibrant, creamy, and deeply flavorful soup made primarily from red lentils. Unlike some heartier lentil stews, Adas has a smoother, often puréed consistency, creating a comforting texture that coats the palate. Its signature taste comes from a harmonious blend of sautéed onions and garlic, the earthy depth of the lentils, and a generous amount of fresh lemon juice added at the end. This citrusy finish is crucial, providing a zesty brightness that elevates the entire dish and cuts through the richness of the lentils. Often enriched with a touch of cumin and a final flourish of fresh cilantro or mint, Adas is a nutritional powerhouse. It’s a beloved dish, found on family tables and restaurant menus across Lebanon and beyond, celebrated for its simplicity, nourishing qualities, and comforting warmth. It’s a versatile soup, enjoyed as a light lunch, a starter, or a hearty main course, particularly during the colder months or during periods like Ramadan.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating an authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of simple, readily available ingredients. The key is quality and freshness, especially when it comes to the aromatics and lemon.

*   **Red Lentils:** 1 cup, dried. Make sure to rinse them thoroughly under cold water before use. Red lentils cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. This forms the aromatic base of the soup.
*   **Garlic:** 3-4 cloves, minced. Garlic is essential for that signature Middle Eastern flavor.
*   **Olive Oil:** 3-4 tablespoons, divided. Use a good quality extra virgin olive oil for sautéing and a drizzle for serving.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** 6-8 cups. While water works perfectly fine, vegetable broth can add an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1/4 to 1/2 cup, freshly squeezed. This is non-negotiable for the authentic Adas taste. Add to taste.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Ground Cumin:** 1 teaspoon (optional, but highly recommended). Cumin complements lentils beautifully.
*   **Fresh Cilantro or Mint:** 1/4 cup, chopped, for garnish (optional).

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Adas Soup

Making Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is surprisingly straightforward. Follow these steps for a delicious and comforting bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it becomes translucent and softened. Do not let it brown too much.
2.  **Add Garlic:** Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the garlic, as this can make it bitter.
3.  **Combine Lentils and Liquid:** Add the thoroughly rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in the vegetable broth or water, and add salt, black pepper, and ground cumin (if using). Stir everything together.
4.  **Simmer:** Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Achieve Desired Consistency:** At this point, the lentils should be very soft. You can leave the soup as is for a slightly chunkier texture, or for a smoother soup, use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup until it reaches your desired consistency. Alternatively, carefully transfer portions of the soup to a regular blender (vent the lid!) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Add Lemon Juice:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice. Start with 1/4 cup and add more gradually until you achieve the perfect balance of tanginess. This step is crucial for the authentic flavor of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup.
7.  **Taste and Adjust:** Taste the soup and adjust seasonings as needed. You might want more salt, pepper, or lemon juice. If the soup is too thick, you can thin it with a little more hot water or broth.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Drizzle each serving with a tablespoon of fresh olive oil and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro or mint, if desired. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that truly authentic and irresistible Lebanese Red Lentil Soup flavor involves a few key techniques:

*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** The fresh lemon juice added at the end is arguably the most important ingredient. It brightens the soup and provides that signature tangy zest. Always use freshly squeezed lemon juice, not bottled.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** A generous drizzle of good quality extra virgin olive oil over the finished soup not only adds richness but also a wonderful peppery note that enhances the overall flavor.
*   **Rinse Your Lentils:** Rinsing red lentils thoroughly before cooking removes any dust or debris and also helps prevent the soup from becoming cloudy.
*   **Cook Until Very Tender:** Ensure the lentils are completely broken down. This is what gives Adas its characteristic creamy, smooth texture. If they're still a bit firm, keep simmering.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning is personal. Don't be afraid to taste the soup multiple times as you cook and adjust salt, pepper, and especially lemon juice to your preference.
*   **Aromatics are Key:** Take your time sautéing the onions until they're soft and translucent. This builds a foundational layer of flavor for your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup.
*   **Garnish Matters:** Fresh herbs like cilantro or mint, along with extra lemon wedges, aren't just for show. They add a burst of freshness and aroma that beautifully complements the hearty soup.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is traditionally served hot, often as a satisfying meal on its own or as a starter. Here are some popular serving suggestions and pairings:

*   **Fresh Pita Bread:** Warm pita bread is the perfect accompaniment for scooping up every last drop of the delicious soup.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always serve with extra lemon wedges on the side, allowing diners to add more tanginess to their individual bowls.
*   **Drizzle of Olive Oil:** A final drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil before serving adds a luxurious finish and enhances the flavor.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro or mint adds a vibrant color and fresh aroma.
*   **Pickles (Mukhalal):** A common side in Lebanese cuisine, assorted pickled vegetables offer a tangy contrast to the soup.
*   **Olives:** A small bowl of olives can also be a delightful addition.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple green salad or a traditional Fattoush salad provides a refreshing counterpoint.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of red pepper flakes or a dash of hot sauce can be added.

## Variations and Dietary Adaptations

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is wonderfully adaptable, allowing for personal touches and dietary considerations:

*   **Add Vegetables:** Enhance the nutritional value and texture by adding finely diced carrots, potatoes, or celery along with the lentils. Spinach or Swiss chard can also be stirred in during the last few minutes of cooking.
*   **Spice it Up:** While traditionally mild, you can add a pinch of turmeric for extra color and an earthy note, or a dash of cayenne pepper for a subtle kick.
*   **Garnish Variations:** Besides fresh herbs, consider crispy fried onions, toasted pita croutons, or a sprinkle of sumac for an extra layer of flavor and texture.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A tiny hint of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky depth.
*   **Dietary Adaptations:** Adas is naturally **vegan** and **gluten-free**, making it suitable for a wide range of diets. Just ensure your vegetable broth is certified gluten-free if necessary. It's also a fantastic source of plant-based protein and dietary fiber, making it an excellent choice for a healthy lifestyle.

## Storage and Reheating

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is one of those dishes that often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld.

*   **Storage:** Once cooled to room temperature, transfer the soup to an airtight container. It will keep beautifully in the refrigerator for 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** Adas freezes exceptionally well. Allow the soup to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or heavy-duty freezer bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating:** Reheat the soup gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until it's heated through. If the soup has thickened considerably in the fridge or freezer (which is common for lentil soups), you may need to add a splash of water or vegetable broth to achieve your desired consistency. Always taste and adjust seasonings, especially lemon juice, after reheating, as flavors can mellow. A fresh drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon will revive it beautifully.

Embrace the comforting simplicity and vibrant flavors of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup. This Adas recipe is more than just a meal; it's an experience that nourishes the body and soul, bringing a taste of authentic Lebanese home cooking right to your table. Enjoy!
